terms.meaning: A fraction with denominator 100, written with the symbol %. x% = x/100.
The price the seller paid for an item.
The price quoted by the shopkeeper, sometimes the MRP.
The price the customer pays after any discount.
The amount of money first invested or borrowed.
Adding the interest to the amount, so that the next interest is worked out on the bigger amount.

items.name: Swapping the two numbers
items.formula: x% of y = y% of x

items.name: Percentages above 100
items.formula: More than 100% means more than the whole

items.name: Increase as a multiplier
items.formula: Increase by r%: multiply by (1 + r/100)
items.example: A 65% increase means 1.65 times the original.

items.name: Profit and loss
items.formula: Profit = SP − CP. Loss = CP − SP.

items.name: Gross and net profit
items.example: Gross profit ₹50000 and expenses ₹5000 give net profit ₹45000.

items.name: Compounding twice a year
items.formula: Half the rate, twice the number of terms

items.name: Falling value
items.example: A ₹20000 TV loses 5% a year: after 1 year, 20000 × 0.95 = ₹19000.

mistakes.text: A percentage change depends on the original amount. If A is 25% more than B, then B is 20% less than A, not 25%. Try B = 100 and A = 125.
30% + 20% off is not 50% off. The second discount applies to the reduced price, so it is 44% off.
Up by 50% and then down by 50% does not return to the start. 100 → 150 → 75.
Before working out a profit percentage, check which base is asked for. On CP ₹500 and SP ₹750, it is 50% on cost, but 33.33% on sales.
